newsitem.title: UK: UK company says has no plans to make West film.
newsitem.headline: UK company says has no plans to make West film.

text.p: A British entertainments company said on Thursday it had no plans to make a controversial film about the lives of serial murderers Fred and Rosemary West.

The announcement by the Portman Entertainment Group came as the British government promised an urgent review of the law after one of its legal officials prompted a storm of protest by selling the company an option to the film rights.

"Whilst I understand the interest that the subject matter of this option has aroused, there are no plans at this time to exploit the rights which Portman have acquired," company chairman John Banks said.
Managing director Tim Buxton added: "As a responsible production company, Portman would review very carefully the apprpriateness of proceeding any further."
Protests erupted after it emerged that the Official Solicitor, the legal official in charge of the West estate, had decided to sell the rights to West's memoirs to Portman.
"It does not feel right, and therefore we need to urgently review this law," said Gary Streeter, a government minister in the office of the Lord Chancellor -- the country's top judge.

"What we need to look at is whether there should be some limit to the commercial exploitation or glorification of the sort of monstrous deeds that have happened in the Fred West case," he told BBC radio.

The duties of the Official Solicitor -- a post currently held by Peter Harris -- include looking after the interests of children, the mentally ill and others who are unable to represent themselves in court proceedings.
Harris said he had a duty to "maximise the financial return to the estate" on behalf of West's five surviving children.

West's older brother Doug said the deal was "sick" and Caroline Roberts, who was sexually abused by the Wests when she was their nanny, said she was worried about what it would do to victims' families.
Fred West was found hanged two years ago in a prison cell where he was awaiting multiple charges of murder.

Many of his victims' bodies were found buried in the garden and cellar of his home at 25 Cromwell Street in Gloucester, western England -- a building so notorious that officials not only knocked it down but ground its bricks into dust.
Rosemary is now serving 10 life sentences for murdering girls and young women.
The option includes access to tape recordings of police interviews with West, tapes of his favourite blue movies and pages of his memoirs written when awaiting trial.
